title: Etale-local parameter-root quotients of invertible-order torsors
statement:
Let $Y$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], $T\subset Y$ a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and $V=Y\setminus|T|$. Let $G$ be a finite group, put $n=|G|$, assume $n$ invertible on $Y$, and let $V'\to V$ be a connected finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose its normalization $b:Z\to Y$ in $k(V')/k(Y)$ is finite [def-fin-normalization-extension, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Fix geometric points $\bar z$ above $\bar y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Then there exist pointed affine etale neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ and $W\to Z$, a map $W\to U$ over $b$, elements $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$ for some $r\ge0$, an element $\zeta\in A^\times$, and a subgroup $H\subseteq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$, with the following properties. The ring $A$ is regular Noetherian and $W$ is Noetherian. The $t_i$ are local equations of precisely the components of $T_U$ through the selected point, belong to its maximal ideal, and form part of a regular system of parameters there [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]; $V\times_Y U=D(t_1\cdots t_r)$. One has $\zeta^n=1$ and $1-\zeta^a\in A^\times$ for $1\le a<n$. For
$$B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),$$
let $H$ act by fixing $A$ and sending $x_i$ to $\zeta^{h_i}x_i$ for $h=(h_i)\in H$. There is an isomorphism $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B^H)$ over $U$, where $B^H=\{b\in B:h(b)=b\text{ for every }h\in H\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Moreover $U$ may be required to refine any prescribed pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar y$ on which the components through $\bar y$ have parameter equations; the $t_i$ can be taken to be the pullbacks of those equations, after shrinking away the other components. The empty boundary gives $r=0$, $B=A$ and $H=0$. No log structure on $Z$ or monoid chart for $b$ is asserted.

source.place: Ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve proof Step 3, uniformization input, through the present item: ILO Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133--134, parameter-root invariant-ring normal form and etale-local reduction; exponent n specialized to the invertible torsor order as in IX 2.2. This is the underlying scheme normal form, including its descent from strict localization to pointed etale neighbourhoods.

proof.text: Begin on an affine pointed neighbourhood of $\bar y$, refining the prescribed one if supplied. The boundary chart gives parameter equations for the components through $\bar y$; remove the other components, so its complement is $D(f)$, $f=\prod_i t_i$. Equations already prescribed differ from these component equations by units locally, so can be used instead. Write this affine ring as $A_0$. Etale algebras over regular rings are regular by smooth ascent. Put $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$, equivalently the strict localization of this neighbourhood. It is regular local by strict-henselization regularity. Its pointed etale-neighbourhood colimit has maximal ideal extended from the point and separably closed residue field. The cotangent-space comparison preserves the independence of the prescribed parameter equations, so their images still extend to a regular system of parameters of $R$.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133, initial strict-local and parameter reduction.

proof.text: Write $Z\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}A_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$. Normalization commutes with this etale (hence smooth) base change, so its restriction to $D(f)$ is the given torsor and it is normal. Finite morphisms over a locally Noetherian base have finite presentation. Let $C=C_0\otimes_{A_0}R$; it is finite over $R$ and hence Noetherian. The henselian finite-algebra product theorem writes $C=\prod_j C_j$ as finite local $R$-algebras. Each $C_j$ is a normal domain: localize at its maximal ideal, view it as the local filtered colimit of pointed etale neighbourhoods over the corresponding local normal domain of $Z$, and apply the etale-colimit normal-domain theorem. Select the factor containing the lift of $\bar z$ and call it $D$. Its generic restriction is one component of the generic torsor: every component dominates the base, since the same holds before etale base change and the normal etale components remain open and closed. Thus $R\hookrightarrow D$, and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ is a finite extension of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, pp.133--134, normalization and strict-local reduction.

proof.text: The roots-of-unity theorem over the strictly henselian ring $R$ gives a generator $\zeta$ of $\mu_n(R)$, with $\zeta^n=1$ and all $1-\zeta^a$ ($0<a<n$) units. Form $\widetilde B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. The simultaneous-root structure theorem makes $\widetilde B$ a regular strictly henselian local domain with the indicated monomial basis and residue field equal to that of $R$. For $E=\operatorname{Frac}(\widetilde B)$ it identifies $\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)$ with $\Gamma=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$, acting by the displayed rotations.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133, simultaneous-root algebra and its root-of-unity action.

proof.text: Apply simultaneous-root torsor splitting to $V'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $D(f)$; its hypotheses are exactly strict henselian regular locality, the parameter equations, and invertibility of $n=|G|$. After base change to $\widetilde B[1/f]$ the entire torsor is a disjoint union of $n$ copies of that base. On the generic point this says that each field factor, in particular $L$, embeds as a $K$-subfield of $E$: an $E$-algebra projection $L\otimes_KE\to E$ restricts to the required embedding $l\mapsto\pi(l\otimes1)$, which is injective because it is unital and $L$ is a field. Fix this embedding.

Let $H\subseteq\Gamma$ consist of the rotations fixing the embedded $L$ pointwise. Since $E/K$ is Galois, the fixed-field theorem gives $E^H=L$. It applies to every intermediate field, so does not require the selected local component to have degree $n$ or the original torsor to stay connected over $R$.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133, the subgroup giving the intermediate cover.

proof.text: Inside $E$, identify $D$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $L$: its elements are integral over $R$ because $D$ is finite, and any element of $L$ integral over $R$ is also integral over $D$, hence in $D$ because $D$ is integrally closed. Likewise $\widetilde B$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $E$, since it is finite and normal. Therefore the integral closure in $L=E^H$ is $\widetilde B\cap E^H=\widetilde B^H$. This gives an isomorphism $D\simeq\widetilde B^H$ of $R$-algebras, and hence of the corresponding finite schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133, invariant ring is the normalization.

proof.text: Descend $\zeta$ to a pointed affine etale neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. Descend also the finitely many equations $\zeta^n=1$ and $(1-\zeta^a)u_a=1$, including the inverse of $\zeta$. Descend the idempotent $e\in C$ cutting out $D$ and the equation $e^2=e$. These are finitely many elements and equalities in the pointed-neighbourhood colimit; after a common refinement all hold. Define $D_1=e(C_0\otimes A_1)$, with identity $e$. It is a direct factor, finite over $A_1$, whose base change to $R$ is $D$. The geometric point $\bar z$ lies in this open-and-closed factor by its selection before descent.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, initial etale locality; finite-data descent from its strict-local calculation.

proof.text: Put $B_1=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. Successive division by these monic polynomials gives the basis $x^a$ ($0\leq a_i<n$) over any coefficient ring: reduce exponents, and uniqueness follows by division in one variable at a time. For $h\in H$, the coefficient of $x^a$ in $h(b)-b$ is $(\zeta^{\sum h_i a_i}-1)b_a$. A nontrivial character value has unit difference from $1$; hence this coefficient vanishes for every $h$ exactly when $b_a=0$ for all noninvariant exponents. Thus $B_1^H$ is free on the invariant basis monomials. This basis description gives $(B_1^H)\otimes_{A_1}R\simeq\widetilde B^H$ by coefficientwise base change. No assertion about arbitrary base change of invariants is needed.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133, diagonal-action invariant algebra; explicit basis calculation.

proof.text: Both $\operatorname{Spec}D_1$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B_1^H)$ are finite over the Noetherian ring $A_1$ and consequently finitely presented; regularity and Noetherianity of $A_1$ follow from smooth ascent. Their base changes to $R$ are isomorphic by Steps 6 and 8. Apply affine finite-presentation isomorphism descent to the ind-etale map $A_1\to R$. It provides an etale $A_1$-algebra $A$ mapping to $R$ on which the two schemes are isomorphic. Pullback of the maximal ideal of $R$ selects a point over $\bar y$; its residue field embeds in the fixed separable closure and hence in the field of $\bar y$, giving the pointed refinement. The basis calculation in Step 8 also identifies the base-changed invariant algebra with $B^H$, for $B=A[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, etale-local reduction; explicit descent of the obtained normal form.

proof.text: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}(D_1\otimes_{A_1}A)$. The projection $Z\times_YU\to Z$ is etale by scheme base change. Its restriction to the open-and-closed affine factor $W$ is etale as well: at each point it has exactly the same local chart and local-ring map as this projection, so the local finite-presentation, flatness and unramifiedness conditions are unchanged. The selected lift of $\bar z$ remains in $W$. The descended isomorphism is $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(B^H)$ over $U$. Finiteness over $A$ gives Noetherianity of $W$. The equations $t_i$ have only been pulled back from $A_0$, and $U$ still avoids every removed component; hence $V_U=D(\prod_i t_i)$ and the parameter requirements hold. When $r=0$, $\Gamma=0$ and the same argument has $\widetilde B=R$, $D=R$, $B=A$ and $H=0$, giving the required etale branch with empty boundary.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, pp.133--134, underlying scheme quotient and etale-local conclusion.
